uncited: *   **Input:** A homogenizing kd-tree representing the volume data, where each node has an associated cost (e.g., number of grid cells or voxels).
*   **Output:** An assignment of each node in the kd-tree to one of the $n$ rendering nodes, and the resulting composite image.
*   **Priority Queue:** A max-heap storing nodes from the kd-tree, ordered by their cost.
The root of the kd-tree is initially the only element.
*   **Subtree Assignment:** A mapping from each kd-tree node to a rendering node ID $0 \dots n-1$.
Assign each node currently in $Q$ (which forms the leaves of the decomposition subtrees) to a unique rendering node.
Each rendering node renders its assigned subtree.
Composite the partial images from the $n$ nodes.
*   Cost metric: Typically the number of voxels or grid cells in the subtree.
*   **Tree Balance:** Good load balancing is contingent on the homogenizing kd-tree being well-balanced.
*   **Insertion Order:** Grids at the same hierarchy level can be inserted into the kd-tree in any order.
*   **Time Complexity:** The decomposition phase takes $O(n \log N)$ where $N$ is the total number of nodes in the kd-tree, assuming a heap operation is $O(\log N)$.
It is part of a suite of algorithms including Cost-range Decomposition and Incremental Load Balancing with Brick Caching.
